faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: What documents do I need to exchange?
faq.a1: For Colombian citizens: national ID (cédula). For foreigners and tourists: valid passport. In all cases we apply full KYC and source-of-funds verification.
faq.q2: Is there a minimum amount to exchange?
faq.a2: No. BitWave does not require a minimum amount. Ask for a quote for the amount you want to exchange and confirm the applicable network fees before sending.
faq.q3: How is the exchange rate calculated?
faq.a3: The quote depends on the amount and market conditions at the time of the transaction, and it is the same for USDT and USDC. You can agree on it with our team on WhatsApp or when you start your negotiation online. Before sending your crypto-assets, confirm the rate, the conditions and the final amount of pesos you will receive.
faq.q4: How long does the operation take?
faq.a4: Identity verification (KYC) normally takes up to 15 minutes. Once verified, the operation generally takes under 5 minutes. Cash pesos are delivered immediately once we confirm receipt of your crypto-assets; bank transfers are processed on the same business day.
faq.q5: Is it legal to exchange crypto-assets in Colombia?
faq.a5: In Colombia crypto-assets are not legal tender and are not supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera, but buying and selling them is not prohibited. BitWave S.A.S. (NIT 901.920.120-1) is a Colombian company, is not supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera, and applies identity verification (KYC), source-of-funds verification and an anti-money laundering system (SARLAFT).
faq.q6: I'm a tourist without a Colombian ID — can you help me?
faq.a6: Yes. We serve international tourists with a valid passport. It is the official document recognized in our KYC process for foreign clients.
faq.q7: Which coins do you trade? Do you accept Bitcoin?
faq.a7: We trade USDT and USDC, on the Polygon, Ethereum, Tron and Solana networks. We do not receive Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies directly, because of the high volatility of those that are not stablecoins. If you hold BTC or another crypto and want pesos, first convert it to USDT or USDC yourself and then exchange it with us. Confirm the network and address with our team before sending.
faq.q8: How do I receive my pesos?
faq.a8: You can receive them in cash at our locations in Oviedo, Viva Envigado and Coltejer, or by bank transfer. Confirm the option when you request your quote.
faq.a9: Zabio is the platform where we carry out our exchanges. Our wallet is there and it is where the USDT and USDC of our clients arrive; that is why clicking "Start negotiation" takes you to zabio.xyz. If you prefer, you can do the whole process on WhatsApp or at our locations.

ratePage.netSub: We receive USDT and USDC on these four networks. Confirm the network and receiving address with our team before sending.
ratePage.netDisclaimer: Costs are approximate and charged by the network, not by BitWave. They change with congestion and the price of the network token. Check them in your wallet before confirming.

polygon.name: Polygon
polygon.cost: Usually costs a few cents of a dollar.
polygon.tip: It uses the same address format as Ethereum. Choose the network carefully when sending.

ethereum.name: Ethereum
ethereum.cost: Can range from around 1 USD to tens of dollars during congestion.
ethereum.fit: Large amounts, where the fee weighs less.
ethereum.tip: Check the fee your wallet shows before confirming.

tron.name: Tron
tron.cost: Roughly 1 to 5 USD, depending on the account energy.
tron.address: Starts with T and has 34 characters.
tron.tip: You need TRX in your wallet to pay the fee.

solana.name: Solana
solana.cost: Usually a fraction of a cent.
solana.address: A string of 32 to 44 characters, no 0x.
solana.fit: Fast transfers with very low fees.
solana.tip: Some wallets ask for a little SOL to pay the fee and to create the token account.

ratePage.guideTitle: How to send crypto-assets between wallets
ratePage.guideSub: A general guide that works for any wallet or exchange.
ratePage.checkBody: Paste the destination address our team gives you and see which network its format belongs to.
ratePage.checkHelp: Everything happens in your browser. We do not store what you paste.
ratePage.checkEmpty: Paste an address to check it.
ratePage.checkEvm: Format compatible with Polygon and Ethereum. It is the same address on both networks, so confirm the network before sending.
ratePage.checkBtc: Bitcoin format. BitWave does not receive Bitcoin directly: convert it to USDT or USDC first.
ratePage.checkUnknown: We do not recognize this format. Check that the address is complete and has no spaces.
ratePage.checkWarn: This only checks the format. It does not confirm that the address exists or that it is the right one.
ratePage.g1t: Choose the crypto-asset and the amount
ratePage.g1d: Decide which coin you are sending, for example USDT or USDC, and how much. Make sure your balance covers the amount and the network fee.
ratePage.g2d: Select in your wallet the network you will send on. It must be the same as the receiving wallet. If they differ, the funds can be lost.
ratePage.g3d: Copy and paste it from an official source. Do not type it by hand.
ratePage.g4d: Compare the first and last characters and confirm that the format matches the chosen network.
ratePage.g5t: Keep a balance for the fee
ratePage.g5d: Each network charges its fee in its own token: POL, ETH, TRX or SOL. Without that balance, the transfer fails.
ratePage.g6d: Before sending, confirm the network, the address and the amount with BitWave. It is our safety step.
ratePage.g7d: Confirm the transfer and save the transaction hash. You can follow it on the network explorer.
ratePage.guideTip: If it is your first time, consider a small test transfer. Keep in mind that each transfer pays its own fee.
ratePage.m1d: It is the most common mistake. An address that starts with 0x exists on several networks: choose the network you agreed on with our team, not the one listed first.
ratePage.m2d: Always paste the address and compare the start and the end.
ratePage.m3t: Not having a balance for the fee
ratePage.m3d: Keep a little of the network token to pay it.
ratePage.m4t: Sharing your seed phrase or private key
ratePage.m4d: BitWave never asks for them. If anyone asks, in our name or anyone else, it is a scam.
ratePage.faqTitle: Questions about the rate and networks
ratePage.f1q: Is the rate I see the final rate?
ratePage.f1a: No. It is an approximate reference. The final rate depends on the crypto-asset, the amount and the market, and is confirmed with our team before you send your crypto-assets.
ratePage.f2a: The one you agree on with our team, and it must be the same as the receiving wallet. We receive USDT and USDC on Polygon, Ethereum, Tron and Solana. Confirm network and address before sending.
ratePage.f3q: What happens if I send on the wrong network?
ratePage.f3a: The funds can be lost or may need a recovery process that is not always possible. That is why we ask you to confirm the network and the address before every transfer.
ratePage.f4q: How much does it cost to send?
ratePage.f4a: The fee is charged by the network, not by BitWave, and it changes with congestion. Polygon and Solana are usually the cheapest. Check the exact cost in your wallet before confirming.
ratePage.f5q: Do I need to register before exchanging?
ratePage.f5a: Identity verification (KYC) is mandatory for everyone. You can do it ahead of time by registering online so your operation moves faster.
ratePage.f6a: No. BitWave does not require a minimum amount. Confirm the quote for the amount you want to exchange.
ratePage.finalBody: Start your negotiation online or message us on WhatsApp and we will guide you.
ratePage.btcLead: We trade only USDT and USDC. We do not receive Bitcoin directly, but you can still get to pesos: you convert it first.
ratePage.btc1t: Convert it to USDT or USDC
ratePage.btc1d: Do it yourself on your exchange or wallet. Check the fees and the rate of that conversion there.
ratePage.btc2t: Send it on the agreed network
ratePage.btc2d: Confirm the network and the address with our team before sending.
ratePage.btc3d: Negotiate with us and receive pesos in cash or by bank transfer.
ratePage.btcWhy: Cryptocurrencies that are not stablecoins are highly volatile: their price can move a lot in a short time, even while the operation is being completed. USDT and USDC are designed to stay pegged to the dollar, which makes clear quoting possible.
ratePage.f7q: Do you accept Bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies?
ratePage.f7a: Not directly. We trade USDT and USDC. If you hold Bitcoin or another crypto, first convert it to USDT or USDC yourself and then exchange it for pesos with us. We do it this way because of the high volatility of cryptocurrencies that are not stablecoins.
